items.question: What is JavaScript?
answer_points: JavaScript is a lightweight, interpreted or just-in-time compiled programming language with first-class functions.
It is most well-known as the scripting language for Web pages, but also used in non-browser environments like Node.js, Apache CouchDB, and Adobe Acrobat.
JavaScript is prototype-based, garbage-collected, and dynamic, supporting imperative, functional, and object-oriented programming paradigms.

Dynamic capabilities include runtime object construction, variable parameter lists, function variables, dynamic script creation via eval, object introspection, and source-code recovery via toString().
JavaScript is standardized as ECMAScript (ECMA-262) and the Internationalization API (ECMA-402).
JavaScript is not related to Java; they have different syntax, semantics, and use.
follow_ups: What are the differences between JavaScript and Java?
Explain the concept of first-class functions in JavaScript.
What is the role of the ECMAScript specification?
items.summary: JavaScript is a versatile, dynamic programming language primarily used for web development.

items.question: What is resource management in JavaScript?
answer_points: Resource management in JavaScript involves handling resources like memory, file handles, and network connections.
The `using` and `await using` declarations provide a way to automatically dispose of resources when they go out of scope.
`DisposableStack` and `AsyncDisposableStack` objects allow for manual management of disposable resources.
Proper resource management helps prevent memory leaks and ensures efficient use of system resources.

items.question: What is internationalization in JavaScript?
answer_points: Internationalization (i18n) in JavaScript refers to designing applications to support multiple languages and regions.
JavaScript provides the `Intl` object for date and time formatting, number formatting, and collation.
Date and time formatting can be done using `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.
Number formatting uses `Intl.NumberFormat` for currency, percentages, etc.
Collation (string comparison) is handled by `Intl.Collator`.

items.summary: JavaScript internationalization uses the `Intl` object for locale-sensitive formatting.

items.question: What are JavaScript modules?
answer_points: JavaScript modules allow you to split code into separate files for better organization and reusability.
Modules use `export` to expose functions, objects, or primitives, and `import` to use them.
Default exports allow a module to export a single value as the default.
Named exports can be renamed using `as` during import.
Modules can be aggregated by re-exporting from other modules.
Dynamic module loading is possible using `import()` which returns a promise.
follow_ups: What is the difference between default and named exports?
How does tree-shaking work with ES modules?
items.summary: JavaScript modules enable code modularity through `export` and `import` statements.

items.question: What are advanced topics in JavaScript?
answer_points: Advanced JavaScript topics include closures, prototypes, inheritance, and memory management.
Closures allow functions to retain access to their lexical scope even when executed outside that scope.
Prototype-based inheritance enables objects to inherit properties and methods from other objects.
Memory management involves understanding garbage collection and avoiding memory leaks.
Meta programming with `Proxy` and `Reflect` allows intercepting and customizing object behavior.
follow_ups: How does JavaScript's prototype chain work?
What are common causes of memory leaks in JavaScript?
items.summary: Advanced JavaScript covers closures, prototypes, memory management, and meta programming.

answer_points: JavaScript is a cross-platform, object-oriented scripting language used to make webpages interactive.
It can run in browsers (client-side) and on servers (e.g., Node.js).
JavaScript has a standard library including objects like Array, Map, and Math.
Client-side JavaScript extends the core language to control the DOM and handle user events.
Server-side JavaScript allows database communication and file manipulation.

items.summary: JavaScript is a versatile scripting language for web development, both client and server side.

items.question: What are the differences between JavaScript and Java?
answer_points: JavaScript is dynamically typed, while Java is statically typed.
JavaScript uses prototype-based inheritance; Java uses class-based inheritance.
JavaScript does not require variable, class, or method declarations; Java does.
JavaScript is more free-form and less complex than Java.
Java is designed for fast execution and type safety.

It ensures consistent behavior across all applications that support the standard.
The specification is maintained by Ecma International and also approved by ISO as ISO-16262.
ECMAScript does not describe the DOM; DOM is standardized by W3C and WHATWG.

items.summary: ECMAScript is the standardized specification that JavaScript implements.

answer_points: JavaScript is case-sensitive and uses Unicode; statements are separated by semicolons (optional with ASI).
Comments can be single-line (//) or multi-line (/* */), but cannot be nested.
Variables are declared using var, let, or const, with different scoping rules.
JavaScript has eight data types: Boolean, null, undefined, Number, BigInt, String, Symbol, and Object.
JavaScript is dynamically typed, allowing automatic type conversion.

items.question: What is the basic syntax and comment syntax in JavaScript?
answer_points: JavaScript syntax is similar to Java and C++; it is case-sensitive and uses Unicode.
Statements are separated by semicolons, but ASI can insert them automatically.
Single-line comments use //, multi-line comments use /* */, and nesting is not allowed.
Hashbang comments (#!) are used to specify the JavaScript engine path.

items.question: What are the different variable declarations in JavaScript?
answer_points: var declares a function-scoped or globally-scoped variable, optionally initialized.
let declares a block-scoped local variable, optionally initialized.
const declares a block-scoped read-only constant that must be initialized.
Variables should always be declared before use; undeclared variables create globals in non-strict mode.
Destructuring allows unpacking values from objects or arrays into variables.
follow_ups: What is the difference between var and let?

items.summary: JavaScript provides var, let, and const for variable declaration with different scopes.

items.question: What is variable scope in JavaScript?
answer_points: Scope determines where a variable is accessible: global, module, function, or block scope.
Variables declared with var are function-scoped, not block-scoped.
Variables declared with let and const are block-scoped.
Global variables are properties of the global object (window in browsers).
Variables should be declared before use to avoid ReferenceError.
follow_ups: What is the difference between function scope and block scope?
How do you access global variables from an iframe?
What is the temporal dead zone?
items.summary: JavaScript has global, module, function, and block scopes, with var being function-scoped.

items.question: What is variable hoisting in JavaScript?
answer_points: Hoisting moves variable declarations to the top of their scope during compilation.
var declarations are hoisted with an initial value of undefined.
let and const are hoisted but not initialized, causing a ReferenceError if accessed before declaration (temporal dead zone).
Function declarations are hoisted entirely, allowing them to be called before their definition.
follow_ups: What is the temporal dead zone?
How does hoisting differ between var, let, and const?
Why is it best practice to declare variables at the top of their scope?
items.summary: Hoisting lifts declarations to the top; var is initialized with undefined, let/const are not.

items.question: What are the data types in JavaScript?
answer_points: JavaScript has eight data types: seven primitives (Boolean, null, undefined, Number, BigInt, String, Symbol) and Object.
JavaScript is dynamically typed, meaning variables can change type.
The '+' operator converts numbers to strings; other operators convert strings to numbers.
Use parseInt(), parseFloat(), Number(), or unary '+' to convert strings to numbers.

items.question: What are literals in JavaScript?
answer_points: Literals are fixed values that appear directly in code, including array, boolean, numeric, object, RegExp, and string literals.
Array literals use square brackets; extra commas create empty slots.
Numeric literals can be decimal, hexadecimal (0x), octal (0o), binary (0b), or BigInt (n suffix).
Object literals use curly braces; property names can be strings or numbers.
String literals can use single or double quotes; template literals use backticks and support interpolation.
RegExp literals are patterns between slashes.

items.summary: Literals are fixed-value representations in JavaScript code, covering arrays, booleans, numbers, objects, regex, and strings.

items.question: How does control flow work in JavaScript?
answer_points: JavaScript uses block statements (curly braces) to group statements.
Conditional statements include if...else and switch.
Exception handling uses try...catch...finally and throw.
Falsy values: false, undefined, null, 0, NaN, empty string; all other values are truthy.
The switch statement matches expression to case labels; break prevents fall-through.
The finally block always executes, even if an exception is thrown or caught.

items.question: How does the if...else statement work in JavaScript?
answer_points: if executes a statement if condition is true; else executes if false.
Use else if for multiple conditions; only the first true condition executes.
Always use block statements {} for clarity, especially when nesting.
Avoid assignments in conditions (e.g., if (x = y)).
Falsy values: false, undefined, null, 0, NaN, ''; all objects are truthy.
Do not confuse primitive booleans with Boolean objects.

items.question: How does the switch statement work in JavaScript?
answer_points: switch evaluates an expression and matches it to case labels.
If a match is found, the associated statements execute until a break or end of switch.
If no match, the default clause executes (if present).
Omitting break causes fall-through to the next case.
The default clause is conventionally last but can be anywhere.
Use switch for multiple discrete value comparisons.

items.summary: switch matches an expression to case labels, with optional default and break to prevent fall-through.

items.question: How does try/catch/throw work in JavaScript?
answer_points: throw statement throws an exception; any expression can be thrown.
try block contains code that may throw; catch block handles exceptions.
finally block always executes after try/catch, regardless of exception.
If finally returns a value, it overrides any return in try/catch.
Nested try/catch: inner try without catch must have finally; outer catch handles uncaught exceptions.
Use Error constructor for meaningful error objects with name and message properties.
follow_ups: What is the difference between throwing a string and an Error object?

items.summary: try/catch/finally handles exceptions; throw raises errors; finally always executes and can override returns.
